items.good: The movie was so boring that I fell asleep.
items.ko: 그 영화는 너무 지루해서 나는 잠이 들었어요.
bad: The movie was so bored that I fell asleep.
The movie was so bore that I fell asleep.
The movie was so bores that I fell asleep.

cz.st: The movie was so ___ that I fell asleep.

items.rule: 사물이 감정을 일으키는 쪽이면 현재분사 -ing를 써요. 영화가 지루함을 일으키므로 boring이에요.
items.hint: 주어가 감정을 일으키는지 느끼는지 생각해 보세요.

items.good: I was surprised to hear the news.
items.ko: 나는 그 소식을 듣고 놀랐어요.
bad: I was surprising to hear the news.
I was surprise to hear the news.
I was surprisingly to hear the news.

cz.st: I was ___ to hear the news.

items.rule: 사람이 놀람을 느끼는 쪽이면 과거분사 -ed를 써요. 소식이 아니라 내가 놀란 것이므로 surprised예요.

items.good: Don't wake the sleeping baby.
items.ko: 잠자는 아기를 깨우지 마세요.
bad: Don't wake the slept baby.
Don't wake the sleeped baby.
Don't wake the to sleep baby.

cz.st: Don't wake the ___ baby.

items.rule: 명사가 직접 하는 동작·상태(자는 중)를 나타낼 때는 현재분사 -ing가 명사 앞에서 꾸며요.

items.good: She picked up the broken glass carefully.
items.ko: 그녀는 깨진 유리를 조심스럽게 주워 들었어요.
bad: She picked up the broke glass carefully.
She picked up the break glass carefully.
She picked up the breaks glass carefully.

cz.st: She picked up the ___ glass carefully.

items.rule: 유리는 깨짐을 당하는 대상이므로 과거분사 broken이 명사 앞에서 '깨진'이라는 뜻으로 꾸며요. broke는 과거형이라 명사를 꾸밀 수 없어요.

items.good: The boy playing the guitar is my cousin.
items.ko: 기타를 치고 있는 소년은 내 사촌이에요.
bad: The boy plays the guitar is my cousin.
The boy played the guitar is my cousin.
The boy play the guitar is my cousin.

cz.st: The boy ___ the guitar is my cousin.

items.rule: 명사 뒤에서 현재분사구가 '~하고 있는'의 뜻으로 꾸밀 수 있어요. 한 문장에 동사가 두 개 나란히 올 수는 없어요.

items.good: The letter written in English was hard to read.
items.ko: 영어로 쓰인 편지는 읽기 어려웠어요.
bad: The letter wrote in English was hard to read.
The letter writes in English was hard to read.
The letter write in English was hard to read.

cz.st: The letter ___ in English was hard to read.

items.rule: 명사 뒤에서 과거분사구가 '~된, ~해진'의 뜻으로 꾸며요. 편지는 쓰이는 대상이라 written이에요.

items.good: I heard my name called from behind.
items.ko: 나는 뒤에서 내 이름이 불리는 소리를 들었어요.
bad: I heard my name calling from behind.
I heard my name call from behind.
I heard my name to call from behind.

cz.st: I heard my name ___ from behind.

items.rule: 지각동사 heard 뒤 목적어가 동작을 당하는 관계이면 목적격 보어로 과거분사를 써요. 이름은 불리는 대상이에요.

items.good: I saw him crossing the road.
items.ko: 나는 그가 길을 건너고 있는 것을 보았어요.
bad: I saw him crossed the road.
I saw him to cross the road.
I saw him crosses the road.

cz.st: I saw him ___ the road.

items.rule: 지각동사 saw 뒤 목적어가 동작을 하는 중이면 목적격 보어로 현재분사를 써요.

items.good: She had her bike repaired yesterday.
items.ko: 그녀는 어제 자전거를 수리받았어요.
bad: She had her bike repair yesterday.
She had her bike repairing yesterday.
She had her bike repairs yesterday.

cz.st: She had her bike ___ yesterday.

items.rule: 사역 표현 have + 목적어 + 과거분사는 '~을 (다른 사람이) ~하게 하다/받다'라는 뜻이에요. 자전거는 수리되는 대상이에요.

items.good: I must get my hair cut before the party.
items.ko: 나는 파티 전에 머리를 잘라야 해요.
bad: I must get my hair cutting before the party.
I must get my hair cutted before the party.
I must get my hair cuts before the party.

cz.st: I must get my hair ___ before the party.

items.rule: get + 목적어 + 과거분사도 '~을 하게 하다/받다'의 뜻이에요. cut은 원형·과거·과거분사의 형태가 모두 같아요.

items.good: Walking along the beach, we found a shell.
items.ko: 해변을 따라 걷다가 우리는 조개껍데기를 발견했어요.
bad: Walked along the beach, we found a shell.
Walks along the beach, we found a shell.
To walking along the beach, we found a shell.

cz.st: ___ along the beach, we found a shell.

items.rule: 분사구문은 '~하면서, ~할 때'의 뜻이에요. 주어(we)가 직접 걷는 능동 관계이므로 현재분사 Walking을 써요.

items.good: Not knowing the answer, he stayed silent.
items.ko: 답을 몰라서 그는 조용히 있었어요.
bad: Not known the answer, he stayed silent.
Not knew the answer, he stayed silent.
Don't knowing the answer, he stayed silent.

cz.st: ___ the answer, he stayed silent.

items.rule: 분사구문의 부정은 분사 바로 앞에 not을 둬요. 주어가 직접 아는(모르는) 능동 관계이므로 Not knowing이에요.

items.good: Seen from the hill, the town looked like a toy.
items.ko: 언덕에서 보면 그 마을은 장난감처럼 보였어요.
bad: Seeing from the hill, the town looked like a toy.
Saw from the hill, the town looked like a toy.
See from the hill, the town looked like a toy.

cz.st: ___ from the hill, the town looked like a toy.

items.rule: 주어(마을)가 보이는 수동 관계이면 과거분사로 시작하는 분사구문을 써요.

items.good: Tired after the long walk, she went to bed early.
items.ko: 긴 산책 후에 피곤해서 그녀는 일찍 잠자리에 들었어요.
bad: Tiring after the long walk, she went to bed early.
Tire after the long walk, she went to bed early.
Tires after the long walk, she went to bed early.

cz.st: ___ after the long walk, she went to bed early.

items.rule: 분사구문에서 'Being'이 생략된 형태예요. 사람이 피곤함을 느끼므로 과거분사 Tired를 써요.

items.good: The students sat quietly with their eyes closed.
items.ko: 학생들은 눈을 감은 채 조용히 앉아 있었어요.
bad: The students sat quietly with their eyes close.
The students sat quietly with their eyes closes.
The students sat quietly with their eyes to close.

cz.st: The students sat quietly with their eyes ___.

items.rule: with + 목적어 + 분사는 '~한 채로'의 뜻이에요. 눈은 감겨지는 수동 관계이므로 과거분사를 써요.

items.good: She ran with her hair tied back.
items.ko: 그녀는 머리를 뒤로 묶은 채 달렸어요.
bad: She ran with her hair tying back.
She ran with her hair tie back.
She ran with her hair ties back.

cz.st: She ran with her hair ___ back.

items.rule: with + 목적어 + 분사에서 머리는 묶이는 대상이므로 과거분사 tied가 알맞아요.

items.good: He spent the whole weekend playing games.
items.ko: 그는 주말 내내 게임을 하며 보냈어요.
bad: He spent the whole weekend play games.
He spent the whole weekend played games.
He spent the whole weekend to play games.

cz.st: He spent the whole weekend ___ games.

items.rule: spend + 시간 + -ing는 '~하면서 시간을 보내다'라는 표현이에요.

items.good: My mother is busy cooking dinner.
items.ko: 어머니는 저녁을 요리하느라 바빠요.
bad: My mother is busy cook dinner.
My mother is busy cooked dinner.
My mother is busy to cook dinner.

cz.st: My mother is busy ___ dinner.

items.rule: be busy + -ing는 '~하느라 바쁘다'라는 표현이에요.

items.good: We went shopping at the mall.
items.ko: 우리는 쇼핑몰에서 쇼핑을 했어요.
bad: We went shop at the mall.
We went shopped at the mall.
We went shops at the mall.

cz.st: We went ___ at the mall.

items.rule: go + -ing는 '~하러 가다'의 뜻으로 운동·여가 활동에 자주 써요.

items.good: I had trouble finding my keys.
items.ko: 나는 열쇠를 찾는 데 어려움을 겪었어요.
bad: I had trouble find my keys.
I had trouble found my keys.
I had trouble finds my keys.

cz.st: I had trouble ___ my keys.

items.rule: have trouble + -ing는 '~하는 데 어려움을 겪다'라는 표현이에요.

items.good: The books left on the desk belong to Jiho.
items.ko: 책상 위에 남겨진 책들은 지호의 것이에요.
bad: The books leaving on the desk belong to Jiho.
The books leave on the desk belong to Jiho.
The books leaves on the desk belong to Jiho.

cz.st: The books ___ on the desk belong to Jiho.

items.rule: 명사 뒤에서 과거분사가 '~된, ~해진'의 뜻으로 꾸며요. 책들은 놓여진(남겨진) 대상이에요.

items.good: The test results were disappointing.
items.ko: 시험 결과는 실망스러웠어요.
bad: The test results were disappointed.
The test results were disappoint.
The test results were disappointment.

cz.st: The test results were ___.

items.rule: 결과(사물)가 실망을 일으키므로 현재분사형 형용사 disappointing을 써요. 실망을 느끼는 쪽은 사람이라 disappointed가 와요.

items.good: Are you interested in space science?
items.ko: 당신은 우주 과학에 관심이 있나요?
bad: Are you interesting in space science?
Are you interest in space science?
Are you interests in space science?

cz.st: Are you ___ in space science?

items.rule: be interested in은 '~에 관심이 있다'라는 표현이에요. 사람이 관심을 느끼므로 interested를 써요.

items.good: My grandfather told us an amazing story about his village.
items.ko: 할아버지는 우리에게 마을에 관한 놀라운 이야기를 해 주셨어요.
bad: My grandfather told us an amazed story about his village.
My grandfather told us an amaze story about his village.
My grandfather told us an amazes story about his village.

cz.st: My grandfather told us an ___ story about his village.

items.rule: 이야기는 놀라움을 일으키는 쪽이므로 amazing이 알맞아요.

items.good: The children were excited about the field trip.
items.ko: 아이들은 현장 학습 때문에 신이 났어요.
bad: The children were exciting about the field trip.
The children were excite about the field trip.
The children were excitement about the field trip.

cz.st: The children were ___ about the field trip.

items.rule: 아이들이 신남을 느끼는 쪽이므로 과거분사형 excited를 써요.

items.good: It was embarrassing to forget his name.
items.ko: 그의 이름을 잊어버린 것은 창피한 일이었어요.
bad: It was embarrassed to forget his name.
It was embarrass to forget his name.
It was embarrasses to forget his name.

cz.st: It was ___ to forget his name.

items.rule: 상황(it)이 창피함을 일으키므로 embarrassing을 써요. 사람이 창피함을 느낄 때는 I was embarrassed처럼 -ed예요.

items.good: The bridge built last year is very safe.
items.ko: 작년에 지어진 다리는 매우 안전해요.
bad: The bridge building last year is very safe.
The bridge build last year is very safe.
The bridge builds last year is very safe.

cz.st: The bridge ___ last year is very safe.

items.rule: 다리는 지어진 대상이므로 명사 뒤에서 과거분사 built가 꾸며요. build의 과거분사는 built예요.

items.good: Having finished my homework, I watched TV.
items.ko: 숙제를 끝낸 뒤 나는 텔레비전을 보았어요.
bad: Have finished my homework, I watched TV.
Having finish my homework, I watched TV.
Had finishing my homework, I watched TV.

cz.st: ___ my homework, I watched TV.

items.rule: 분사구문에서 주절보다 앞선 일은 having + 과거분사로 나타내요.

items.good: Born in a small village, she dreamed of seeing the world.
items.ko: 작은 마을에서 태어난 그녀는 세상을 보는 꿈을 꾸었어요.
bad: Bearing in a small village, she dreamed of seeing the world.
Bore in a small village, she dreamed of seeing the world.
Bear in a small village, she dreamed of seeing the world.

cz.st: ___ in a small village, she dreamed of seeing the world.

items.rule: '태어나다'는 be born으로 수동의 뜻이에요. 분사구문에서는 Born으로 시작해요.

items.good: The woman sitting next to me kept coughing.
items.ko: 내 옆에 앉아 있는 여자는 계속 기침을 했어요.
bad: The woman sat next to me kept coughing.
The woman sits next to me kept coughing.
The woman sit next to me kept coughing.

cz.st: The woman ___ next to me kept coughing.

items.rule: 명사 뒤에 현재분사구가 오면 '~하고 있는'의 뜻으로 그 명사를 꾸며요.

items.good: Please keep the door closed.
items.ko: 문을 닫아 둔 채로 유지해 주세요.
bad: Please keep the door closing.
Please keep the door closes.
Please keep the door to close.

cz.st: Please keep the door ___.

items.rule: keep + 목적어 + 과거분사는 '~을 ~된 상태로 두다'라는 뜻이에요.

items.good: The teacher kept us waiting for an hour.
items.ko: 선생님은 우리를 한 시간 동안 기다리게 했어요.
bad: The teacher kept us wait for an hour.
The teacher kept us waited for an hour.
The teacher kept us to wait for an hour.

cz.st: The teacher kept us ___ for an hour.

items.rule: keep + 목적어 + 현재분사는 '~을 계속 ~하게 두다'라는 뜻이에요.

items.good: I felt my phone vibrating in my pocket.
items.ko: 나는 주머니에서 휴대 전화가 진동하는 것을 느꼈어요.
bad: I felt my phone vibrated in my pocket.
I felt my phone vibrates in my pocket.
I felt my phone to vibrate in my pocket.

cz.st: I felt my phone ___ in my pocket.

items.rule: 지각동사 felt 뒤 목적어가 하는 중인 동작은 목적격 보어로 현재분사를 써요.

items.good: We watched the sun going down behind the hills.
items.ko: 우리는 해가 언덕 뒤로 지는 것을 지켜보았어요.
bad: We watched the sun gone down behind the hills.
We watched the sun goes down behind the hills.
We watched the sun to go down behind the hills.

cz.st: We watched the sun ___ down behind the hills.

items.rule: watch + 목적어 + 현재분사는 진행 중인 장면을 지켜본다는 뜻이에요.

items.good: The company produces frozen food.
items.ko: 그 회사는 냉동식품을 생산해요.
bad: The company produces freeze food.
The company produces froze food.
The company produces freezes food.

cz.st: The company produces ___ food.

items.rule: 음식은 얼려지는 대상이므로 과거분사 frozen이 명사 앞에서 '냉동된'이라는 뜻으로 꾸며요.

items.good: I bought a used bike at a low price.
items.ko: 나는 낮은 가격에 중고 자전거를 샀어요.
bad: I bought a using bike at a low price.
I bought a use bike at a low price.
I bought a to use bike at a low price.

cz.st: I bought a ___ bike at a low price.

items.rule: used는 '사용된, 중고의'라는 뜻의 과거분사형 형용사예요.

items.good: I had a boiled egg for breakfast.
items.ko: 나는 아침으로 삶은 달걀을 먹었어요.
bad: I had a boiling egg for breakfast.
I had a boil egg for breakfast.
I had a boils egg for breakfast.

cz.st: I had a ___ egg for breakfast.

items.rule: 달걀은 삶아지는 대상이므로 과거분사 boiled가 알맞아요.

items.good: Given more time, I could finish the project.
items.ko: 시간이 더 주어진다면 나는 그 프로젝트를 끝낼 수 있을 거예요.
bad: Giving more time, I could finish the project.
Gave more time, I could finish the project.
Give more time, I could finish the project.

cz.st: ___ more time, I could finish the project.

items.rule: 분사구문이 '~이 주어진다면'이라는 조건을 나타내고, 주어가 주어지는 수동 관계이므로 Given을 써요.

items.good: Compared with my brother, I am short.
items.ko: 내 남동생과 비교하면 나는 키가 작아요.
bad: Comparing with my brother, I am short.
Compare with my brother, I am short.
Compares with my brother, I am short.

cz.st: ___ with my brother, I am short.

items.rule: 주어(I)가 비교되는 수동 관계이므로 과거분사 Compared로 분사구문을 시작해요.

items.good: Judging from the clouds, it will rain soon.
items.ko: 구름으로 판단하건대 곧 비가 올 거예요.
bad: Judge from the clouds, it will rain soon.
Judges from the clouds, it will rain soon.
Being judge from the clouds, it will rain soon.

cz.st: ___ from the clouds, it will rain soon.

items.rule: judging from은 '~로 판단하건대'라는 뜻으로 굳어진 분사구문 표현이에요.

items.good: The stolen bike was found near the river.
items.ko: 도난당한 자전거는 강 근처에서 발견되었어요.
bad: The stealing bike was found near the river.
The steal bike was found near the river.
The stole bike was found near the river.

cz.st: The ___ bike was found near the river.

items.rule: 자전거는 도난당한 대상이므로 과거분사 stolen이 알맞아요. steal - stole - stolen 순으로 변해요.

items.good: The guests invited to the party brought small gifts.
items.ko: 파티에 초대받은 손님들은 작은 선물을 가져왔어요.
bad: The guests invite to the party brought small gifts.
The guests invites to the party brought small gifts.
The guests invitation to the party brought small gifts.

cz.st: The guests ___ to the party brought small gifts.

items.rule: 명사 뒤 과거분사구가 '~된, ~받은'의 뜻으로 꾸며요. 손님들은 초대받은 대상이에요.

items.good: Excited by the news, she called her friend at once.
items.ko: 소식에 신이 나서 그녀는 즉시 친구에게 전화했어요.
bad: Exciting by the news, she called her friend at once.
Excite by the news, she called her friend at once.
Excites by the news, she called her friend at once.

cz.st: ___ by the news, she called her friend at once.

items.rule: 그녀가 신남을 느끼는 수동·감정 관계이므로 과거분사로 시작하는 분사구문을 써요.

items.good: The teacher, loved by all her students, retired last spring.
items.ko: 모든 학생에게 사랑받던 그 선생님은 지난봄에 퇴직했어요.
bad: The teacher, loving by all her students, retired last spring.
The teacher, love by all her students, retired last spring.
The teacher, loves by all her students, retired last spring.

cz.st: The teacher, ___ by all her students, retired last spring.

items.rule: '~에 의해 사랑받는'처럼 by가 뒤따르는 수동 의미에는 과거분사를 써요.

items.good: She sat in the garden reading a magazine.
items.ko: 그녀는 잡지를 읽으며 정원에 앉아 있었어요.
bad: She sat in the garden reads a magazine.
She sat in the garden readed a magazine.
She sat in the garden be reading a magazine.

cz.st: She sat in the garden ___ a magazine.

items.rule: 동시에 일어나는 동작은 현재분사로 덧붙여 '~하면서'의 뜻을 나타낼 수 있어요.

items.good: Left alone in the room, the baby began to cry.
items.ko: 방에 혼자 남겨지자 아기는 울기 시작했어요.
bad: Leaving alone in the room, the baby began to cry.
Leave alone in the room, the baby began to cry.
Leaves alone in the room, the baby began to cry.

cz.st: ___ alone in the room, the baby began to cry.

items.rule: 아기는 남겨지는 대상이므로 과거분사 Left로 분사구문을 시작해요. leave - left - left로 변해요.

items.q: Which sentence contains a present participle used as an adjective before a noun?
o: She was invited to the party.
items.why: smiling은 명사 teacher를 앞에서 꾸미는 현재분사예요. playing은 진행형 동사의 일부, finished와 invited는 완료형·수동태의 일부예요.

items.q: Choose the sentence in which a past participle is used as an adjective before a noun.
o: I'm looking for a lost wallet.
items.why: lost는 명사 wallet을 앞에서 꾸미는 과거분사형 형용사(잃어버린)예요. closed, played, asked는 과거형 동사이고 difficult는 분사가 아니에요.

items.q: The news about the storm was very ____ to the sailors.
items.why: 뉴스가 두려움을 일으키는 쪽이므로 현재분사형 frightening이 알맞아요. 두려움을 느끼는 선원이 주어라면 frightened를 써요.

items.q: Mina felt very ____ when her friend forgot her birthday.
items.why: 미나가 실망을 느끼는 쪽이므로 과거분사형 disappointed예요. feel 뒤에는 형용사가 와요.

items.q: Find the part that must be changed: “The girl was very interesting in the old map.”
items.why: 소녀가 관심을 느끼는 쪽이므로 interesting이 아니라 interested(be interested in)가 되어야 해요.

items.q: What is the best Korean meaning of “the people living next door”?
o: 곧 옆집으로 이사 올 예정인 사람들
items.why: 명사 뒤 현재분사구 living next door는 '옆집에 살고 있는'이라는 뜻으로 people을 꾸며요.

items.q: “달걀 프라이”를 뜻하는 가장 자연스러운 영어 표현은?
items.why: 달걀은 기름에 튀겨지는(부쳐지는) 대상이므로 과거분사 fried를 써서 a fried egg라고 해요.

items.q: “흐르는 물, 수돗물”을 뜻하는 영어 표현으로 알맞은 것은?
items.why: running water는 '흐르는 물'이라는 뜻으로, running이 명사를 앞에서 꾸미는 현재분사예요.

items.q: Which sentence has the same meaning as “Because I felt sick, I stayed home”?
o: To feeling sick, I stayed home.
items.why: 접속사와 주어를 줄이고 동사를 -ing로 바꾸면 이유를 나타내는 분사구문 Feeling sick이 돼요.

items.q: Which sentence has the same meaning as “When she saw the snow, she shouted with joy”?
o: Seen the snow, she shouted with joy.
See the snow, she shouted with joy.
Saw the snow, she shouted with joy.
Seeing the snow, she shouted with joy.
items.why: 주어 she가 직접 보는 능동 관계이므로 Seeing으로 시작하는 분사구문을 써요.

items.q: Which sentence has the same meaning as “As he was told to wait, he sat down”?
o: Telling to wait, he sat down.
Tell to wait, he sat down.
Told to wait, he sat down.
Be tell to wait, he sat down.
items.why: he는 말을 듣는(지시받는) 수동 관계이므로 Being이 생략된 과거분사 Told로 시작해요.

items.q: Which sentence has the same meaning as “After he had finished his work, he went out”?
o: Having finish his work, he went out.
Having finished his work, he went out.
Had finishing his work, he went out.
Be finished his work, he went out.
items.why: 주절보다 앞선 일은 having + 과거분사로 나타내요.

items.q: Which is the closest meaning of “Not wanting to be late, he ran to the station”?
o: Although he did not want to be late, he ran to the station.
If he did not want to be late, he ran to the station.
Because he did not want to be late, he ran to the station.
After he did not want to be late, he ran to the station.
items.why: 분사구문 Not wanting ...은 여기서 이유(~하고 싶지 않아서)를 나타내요.

items.q: Which expression means “일반적으로 말하자면”?
items.why: Generally speaking은 '일반적으로 말하면'이라는 뜻으로 굳어진 분사구문 표현이에요.

items.q: In “Considering his age, he runs very fast,” the word Considering means ____.
items.why: considering은 '~을 고려하면, ~치고는'의 뜻으로 쓰이는 분사구문 표현이에요.

items.q: We listened to the birds ____ in the trees.
items.why: 지각동사 listen to 뒤에서 새들이 노래하고 있는 능동·진행 장면이므로 현재분사 singing이 알맞아요. listen to 뒤에는 that절이 올 수 없어서 sang, sings는 틀려요.

items.q: Which sentence means “그는 버스에서 지갑을 도난당했다”?
o: He had his wallet stealing on the bus.
He had his wallet stolen on the bus.
He had his wallet steal on the bus.
He had his wallet to steal on the bus.
items.why: have + 목적어 + 과거분사는 '~을 당하다/받다'의 뜻도 나타내요. 지갑은 도난당하는 대상이므로 stolen이에요.

items.q: Eun-ji spent two hours ____ her room.
items.why: spend + 시간 + -ing는 '~하는 데 시간을 보내다'라는 표현이에요.

items.q: Which is the correct -ing form of “swim”?
items.why: 짧은 모음 하나와 자음 하나로 끝나는 단어는 자음을 한 번 더 쓰고 -ing를 붙여요.

items.q: Which is the correct -ing form of “make”?
items.why: -e로 끝나는 동사는 e를 빼고 -ing를 붙여요.

items.q: Which is the correct -ing form of “lie” (눕다)?
items.why: -ie로 끝나는 동사는 ie를 y로 바꾸고 -ing를 붙여요.

items.q: Which is the past participle of “write”?
items.why: write - wrote - written으로 변해요. wrote는 과거형이에요.

items.q: Which is the past participle of “choose”?
items.why: choose - chose - chosen으로 변해요.

items.q: Which is the past participle of “hide”?
items.why: hide - hid - hidden으로 변해요.

items.q: Which is the past participle of “forget”?
items.why: forget - forgot - forgotten으로 변해요.

items.q: The movie was ____, so we were all ____.
items.why: 영화는 감동을 주는 쪽이므로 touching, 사람은 감동을 받는 쪽이므로 touched예요.

items.q: Our trip was ____, and we were ____ after it.
items.why: 여행은 피곤함을 일으키므로 tiring, 사람은 피곤함을 느끼므로 tired예요.

items.q: Which sentence uses the word “amazed” correctly?
o: His magic tricks were amazed by us.
We were amazed by his magic tricks.
The amazed show made us laugh a lot.
Amazed the tricks, we clapped loudly.
items.why: amazed는 놀람을 느끼는 사람을 설명해요. We were amazed by ...가 올바른 문장이에요.

items.q: Which sentence uses the word “annoying” correctly?
o: I felt annoying when the phone rang.
The annoyed noise woke me up early.
My sister is annoyed to sing loudly.
The noise next door is really annoying.
items.why: 소음처럼 짜증을 일으키는 대상에는 annoying을 써요. 사람이 짜증을 느끼면 annoyed예요.

items.q: Which phrase has the same meaning as “the man who is waiting at the gate”?
o: the man had waited at the gate
the man waiting at the gate
the man waits at the gate
the man to wait at the gate
items.why: 관계대명사 + be동사를 줄이면 현재분사구가 명사 뒤에서 꾸며요.

items.q: Which phrase has the same meaning as “the books that were written by Jina”?
items.why: 수동의 뜻인 '쓰인 책들'은 과거분사 written을 써서 나타내요.

items.q: Combine the sentences: “The girl is my cousin. She is reading under the tree.”
o: The girl read under the tree is my cousin.
The girl is reading under the tree is my cousin.
The girl reads under the tree is my cousin.
The girl reading under the tree is my cousin.
items.why: She is reading을 현재분사구 reading under the tree로 바꿔 girl 뒤에서 꾸미게 해요.

items.q: Combine the sentences: “We climbed a hill. It was covered with snow.”
o: We climbed a hill covering with snow.
We climbed a hill cover with snow.
We climbed a hill covered with snow.
We climbed a hill covers with snow.
items.why: 언덕은 눈으로 덮여진 대상이므로 과거분사구 covered with snow가 hill을 꾸며요.

items.q: After the long exam, I felt ____ and wanted to rest.
items.why: 내가 지친 감정·상태를 느끼므로 과거분사형 exhausted예요.

items.q: Her speech was so ____ that everybody wanted to hear more.
items.why: 연설이 사람들을 매료시키는 쪽이므로 fascinating이에요.

items.q: The kids were ____ of the loud thunder.
items.why: be scared of는 '~을 무서워하다'라는 표현이에요. 아이들이 두려움을 느끼므로 scared예요.

items.q: In “Opening the box, Minho found a small key,” who opened the box?
items.why: 분사구문의 의미상 주어는 주절의 주어와 같아요. 따라서 상자를 연 사람은 Minho예요.

items.q: Which sentence has a participle phrase that gives a reason?
o: She put on a coat and a scarf.
Feeling cold, she put on a coat.
Cold weather came early this year.
The coat she bought was cheap.
items.why: Feeling cold는 '추워서'라는 이유를 나타내는 분사구문이에요.

items.q: In “Cooking dinner, Dad listened to the radio,” what does “Cooking” show?
o: an earlier action that had ended
a wish that did not come true
something happening at the same time
items.why: 분사구문은 '~하면서'라는 동시 동작을 나타낼 수 있어요.

items.q: 다음 문장을 바르게 고친 것은? “Everyone was shocking at the news.”
o: Everyone was shock at the news.
Everyone were shocking at the news.
Everyone was shocked at the news.
Everyone was shocks at the news.
items.why: 사람들이 충격을 느끼는 쪽이므로 shocked가 알맞아요. everyone은 단수 취급해요.

items.q: 다음 문장을 바르게 고친 것은? “The excited news made us dance.”
o: The exciting news made us dance.
The excite news made us dance.
The excitement news made us dance.
The excites news made us dance.
items.why: 소식이 흥분을 일으키는 쪽이므로 exciting이 알맞아요.

items.q: “중고차”를 뜻하는 가장 알맞은 표현은?
items.why: used는 '사용된, 중고의'라는 뜻의 과거분사형 형용사예요.

items.q: “말린 과일”을 뜻하는 가장 알맞은 표현은?
items.why: 과일은 말려진 대상이므로 과거분사 dried를 써요.

items.q: “구운 생선”을 뜻하는 가장 알맞은 표현은?
items.why: 생선은 구워지는 대상이므로 과거분사 grilled를 써요.

items.q: Which is the past participle of “bring”?
items.why: bring - brought - brought로 변해요.

items.q: Which is the past participle of “begin”?
items.why: begin - began - begun으로 변해요. began은 과거형이에요.

items.q: Which is the past participle of “speak”?
items.why: speak - spoke - spoken으로 변해요.

items.q: Which sentence uses “surprising” as an adjective that describes a thing?
o: I was surprising by the ending.
We surprising the end of the film.
The surprising people watched the film.
It was a surprising ending to the film.
items.why: surprising은 놀라움을 일으키는 사물·사건을 설명해요.

items.q: In “the hidden treasure,” what does “hidden” mean?
items.why: hidden은 hide의 과거분사로, 명사 앞에서 '숨겨진'이라는 수동의 뜻을 나타내요.

items.q: What is the best Korean meaning of “the barking dog”?
items.why: 현재분사 barking이 명사 dog을 앞에서 꾸며 '짖고 있는, 짖는'이라는 뜻이 돼요.

items.q: In which phrase does the noun RECEIVE the action?
items.why: washed car는 '세차된 차'로 차가 씻김을 받아요. washing machine은 씻기 위한 기계, running boy와 sleeping dog은 명사가 직접 동작을 해요.

items.q: In which phrase does the noun DO the action?
items.why: barking dog은 개가 짖는 동작을 직접 해요. 나머지는 명사가 동작을 당하는 과거분사 표현이에요.

items.q: Which sentence uses “satisfied” correctly?
o: The customers were satisfying with the service.
The customers were satisfied with the service.
The service was satisfied for the customers.
The customers were satisfy with the service.
items.why: 고객이 만족을 느끼는 쪽이므로 satisfied를 써요. 서비스가 만족을 주는 쪽이라면 satisfying이에요.

items.q: There is some pizza ____ in the box.
items.why: 피자는 남겨진 대상이므로 명사 뒤에서 과거분사 left가 꾸며요.

items.q: The workers ____ the bridge are from a local company.
items.why: 일꾼들이 직접 수리하고 있는 능동·진행 관계이므로 현재분사 repairing이 명사를 꾸며요.

items.q: She was ____ her homework when the phone rang.
items.why: was + 현재분사 doing은 과거진행형으로 '하고 있었다'라는 뜻이에요.

items.title: A Rainy Saturday
items.text: It was a rainy Saturday, and my little brother was bored. Sitting by the window, he watched the falling rain and sighed. Mom, tired after a busy week, was resting on the sofa. I had an idea. I found some old boxes stored under the stairs and said, "Let's build a castle!" Soon the living room was filled with laughing, cutting and taping. When Dad came home, he saw two excited kids standing proudly next to a very strange castle. Even Mom, surprised by our work, smiled and joined us.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: A family moves to a new home because of heavy rain.
A mother teaches her sons how to cook a big dinner.
Two children make a rainy day fun with boxes.
A father repairs the roof while his children sleep.
qs.why: 비 오는 날 지루해하던 두 아이가 상자로 성을 만들며 즐겁게 보낸다는 내용이에요.

qs.q: Why was the narrator's little brother bored?
o: He had to stay in because of the rain.
He was sick and needed to see a doctor.
His mother did not let him use the sofa.
He had already finished building his toys.
qs.why: 비 오는 토요일이라 밖에 나가 놀 수 없어서 지루해했다고 추론할 수 있어요.

qs.q: Where did the narrator find the boxes?
qs.why: 본문에서 'old boxes stored under the stairs'라고 했어요.

qs.q: How did Mom probably feel at the end of the story?
o: Angry about the mess in the room
Bored with the castle after a while
Pleased and ready to join the fun
qs.why: 놀라워하며 미소 짓고 함께했다는 표현에서 기뻐했음을 알 수 있어요.

items.title: The Recycling Club
items.text: Last year, our school started a recycling club. At first, only five students joined, but the club kept growing. Every Friday, members collect used paper and broken plastic toys from the classrooms. The sorted materials are then taken to a recycling center by a parent volunteer. Last month, the club made a surprising discovery: our school produced almost half a ton of paper waste in one semester! Shocked by this number, the principal asked every class to use both sides of the paper. Now, the club is planning a poster contest to encourage even more students to help.

qs.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
o: A school is planning to build a new library.
A student club is helping the school reduce waste.
Students are learning how to make paper at home.
A parent volunteer is looking for a better job.
qs.why: 재활용 동아리의 활동과 그 결과(학교의 종이 사용 줄이기)가 글의 중심 내용이에요.

qs.q: When do the club members collect the materials?
o: On the last day of each month
qs.why: 본문에서 'Every Friday, members collect...'라고 했어요.

qs.q: What does “this number” refer to?
o: The amount of paper the school wasted
The number of students who joined first
The number of classes in the school
The number of posters in the contest
qs.why: 바로 앞 문장의 'almost half a ton of paper waste'를 가리켜요.

qs.q: Why did the principal ask classes to use both sides of the paper?
o: To save money on the school lunch program
To make the recycling center smaller
To help students write more neatly
To cut down on paper waste
qs.why: 종이 쓰레기 양에 놀라 낭비를 줄이려는 조치라고 추론할 수 있어요.

qs.q: What is the purpose of the poster contest?
o: To choose the best teacher of the year
To get more students interested in recycling
To raise money for new classroom desks
To find a name for the school club
qs.why: 본문에서 더 많은 학생들이 도와주도록 격려하려고 계획했다고 했어요.

items.title: A Surprising Letter
items.text: Last week, Hana found a letter hidden inside an old book at the library. The paper was yellowed and the writing was faded, but she could still read it. The letter, written fifty years ago by a student, said, "If you are reading this, please plant a tree for me." Hana was amazed. She showed the letter to the librarian, who smiled and said that the school garden needed more trees anyway. On Saturday, Hana and her friends planted a small apple tree near the library door. They put the old letter in a frame and hung it on the wall, so that every visitor could read it.

qs.q: What did the writer of the letter ask the reader to do?
qs.why: 편지에 'please plant a tree for me'라고 쓰여 있었어요.

qs.q: Why did the librarian smile?
o: She had written the letter herself long ago.
She wanted Hana to leave the library quickly.
The idea fit the school's garden plans.
She thought the paper looked very expensive.
qs.why: 정원에 나무가 더 필요하다는 말에서 편지의 부탁이 마침 학교 사정과 맞았다고 추론할 수 있어요.

qs.q: In the passage, the word “faded” is closest in meaning to ____.
qs.why: faded는 색이나 글씨가 흐릿해진 상태를 뜻해요.

qs.q: What does “it” refer to in the last sentence?
qs.why: 앞에서 편지를 액자에 넣어 벽에 걸었다고 했으므로 방문객이 읽을 수 있는 것은 편지예요.

items.title: Sleep and School
items.text: Sleeping well is one of the most important habits for teenagers. Doctors say that students need about eight to ten hours of sleep each night. However, many of us stay up late, watching videos or chatting with friends. Tired students often have trouble concentrating in class, and they may feel worried or angry for no reason. To sleep better, try turning off your phone an hour before bed. Reading a printed book or listening to quiet music can also help. Small changes like these will leave you feeling refreshed in the morning.

qs.q: Why did the writer write this passage?
o: To advertise a new kind of phone
To tell a funny story about a late night
To give advice about sleeping better
qs.why: 수면 습관의 중요성을 말하고 잠을 잘 자는 방법을 조언하는 글이에요.

qs.q: How long before bed does the writer suggest turning off the phone?
qs.why: 본문에서 'turning off your phone an hour before bed'라고 했어요.

qs.q: Which of the following is NOT mentioned as a way to sleep better?
qs.why: 따뜻한 우유는 언급되지 않았어요.

qs.q: According to the passage, what can happen to students who are tired?
o: They always get the highest scores.
They never feel hungry at lunch.
They may find it hard to focus in class.
They grow taller than other students.
qs.why: 피곤한 학생은 수업 중 집중하기 어렵다(trouble concentrating)고 했어요.

items.title: The Night Market
items.text: Day 3. Tonight we visited the night market in the small coastal town where we are staying. The streets were crowded with people holding paper lanterns, and the smell of grilled fish and fried dumplings was everywhere. My sister bought a hand-painted fan from a smiling old woman, while I tried some sweet, frozen fruit on a stick. Although I was exhausted from the long bus ride, I didn't want to leave. Next time, I will bring more money! We went back to the hotel at ten, tired but satisfied.

qs.q: What type of writing is this passage?
qs.why: Day 3로 시작하고 하루의 경험과 느낌을 적고 있으므로 여행 일기예요.

qs.q: What did the writer's sister buy?
qs.why: 본문에서 여동생이 hand-painted fan을 샀다고 했어요. 얼린 과일은 글쓴이가 먹었어요.

qs.q: Why does the writer say, “Next time, I will bring more money”?
o: The bus driver asked for extra money.
He or she lost a wallet at the market.
He or she wanted to buy more things.
qs.why: 시장에서 더 사고 싶었다는 아쉬움을 암시해요.

qs.q: How did the writer feel at the end of the night?
qs.why: 'tired but satisfied'로 끝나며, 피곤하지만 만족했음을 알 수 있어요.

qs.q: In the passage, “crowded with” is closest in meaning to ____.
qs.why: crowded with는 '~로 붐비는, 가득한'의 뜻이에요.

items.title: Our Robot Vacuum
items.text: My family bought a robot vacuum last month. At first, my dog was frightened of the spinning machine and hid under the bed. But after a few days, he became curious and started following it around the house. The vacuum is not perfect. Sometimes it gets stuck under the sofa, and we have to rescue it. Still, my mother says that coming home to a clean floor is wonderful. The only problem is that my brother now leaves his socks everywhere and says, "The robot will take care of it!" Of course, it won't.

qs.q: How did the dog react to the robot vacuum at first?
o: He barked and chased it outside.
He hid because he was scared.
He jumped on top of it happily.
He ignored it and kept sleeping.
qs.why: 처음에는 겁을 먹고 침대 밑에 숨었다고 했어요.

qs.q: What does “it” in “we have to rescue it” refer to?
qs.why: 소파 밑에 끼는 것은 로봇 청소기예요.

qs.q: What can we guess about the brother?
o: He expects the robot to fix his mess.
He wants to sell the robot to a neighbor.
He is afraid of the dog and the machine.
He cleans the whole house every day.
qs.why: 양말을 아무 데나 두고 로봇이 해결할 거라고 말하는 모습에서 추론할 수 있어요.

qs.q: What is the writer's attitude toward the robot vacuum?
qs.why: 장점을 인정하면서도 재미있게 단점을 말하고 있어요.

items.title: Grandfather's Garden
items.text: My grandfather has a small garden behind his house. Early every morning, he walks among the growing vegetables, checking each plant. He says that tomatoes grown with patience taste better than any bought in a store. This summer, he taught me how to tie the climbing beans to wooden sticks and how to water the plants without wasting a drop. At first, I felt bored, but slowly I became interested in the work. When we ate our first salad made from the garden, I understood why Grandfather smiles so much while working.

qs.q: What did Grandfather teach the writer to do?
o: Sell fresh tomatoes at a local store
Build a small wooden house for birds
Pick wild flowers for a big vase
Tie climbing beans to wooden sticks
qs.why: 본문에서 콩 줄기를 나무 막대에 묶는 법을 가르쳤다고 했어요.

qs.q: How did the writer's feeling change?
qs.why: 처음에는 지루했지만 점차 흥미를 느꼈다고 했어요.

qs.q: Why does Grandfather probably smile so much while working?
o: He is waiting for visitors to arrive.
He has just won a gardening prize.
He plans to move to a bigger house.
qs.why: 직접 기른 채소로 샐러드를 먹은 뒤 이유를 이해했다는 흐름에서 추론할 수 있어요.

qs.q: In the passage, “patience” is closest in meaning to ____.
qs.why: patience는 서두르지 않고 차분히 기다리는 태도를 뜻해요.

items.title: Spring Festival Notice
items.text: Attention, students! The Spring Festival will be held on Friday, May 9, in the main gym. Doors open at 1 p.m. Performances include a dance by the Hip-Hop Club, a short play written and acted by Class 3-2, and a concert played by the school band. Students interested in joining the cooking contest should sign up at the front desk by Wednesday. Please remember to bring a reusable water bottle, because plastic cups will not be provided this year. Parents are welcome, but all visitors must wear a name tag given at the entrance.

qs.q: What is the purpose of this notice?
o: To ask students to clean the gym
To announce the winners of a contest
To give information about a school event
To invite teachers to a meeting
qs.why: 축제 날짜, 장소, 프로그램과 준비물을 알리는 안내문이에요.

qs.q: How can a student join the cooking contest?
o: By calling the school band leader on Friday
By signing up at the front desk by Wednesday
By coming to the gym at 1 p.m. that day
By bringing a name tag to the entrance
qs.why: 본문에서 수요일까지 안내 데스크에서 신청하라고 했어요.

qs.q: Why should students bring a reusable water bottle?
o: The school will not offer plastic cups.
The gym has no water at all.
The band needs bottles for a game.
Parents must bring their own food.
qs.why: 플라스틱 컵이 제공되지 않는다고 했으므로 개인 물병이 필요해요.

qs.q: Who wrote the short play?
qs.why: 'a short play written and acted by Class 3-2'라고 했어요.

items.title: The Lost Puppy
items.text: Jun was walking home when he heard a weak sound coming from behind a trash can. He looked closer and found a small dog shaking with cold. The frightened puppy had no collar, and its fur was wet. Jun took off his jacket, wrapped the puppy in it, and carried it home. His mother, worried at first, finally agreed to let the dog stay for a night. The next day, they put up posters with the puppy's picture. Two days later, a girl called, crying with joy. "That's my dog, Coco!" she said. Jun felt happy, but also a little sad.

qs.q: What did Jun do right after he found the puppy?
o: He wrapped it in his jacket.
He put up posters on the street.
qs.why: 재킷을 벗어 강아지를 감싸 집으로 데려갔어요.

qs.q: Why was Jun's mother worried at first?
o: She was afraid of the cold weather outside.
She had lost her own dog the week before.
She disliked the color of Jun's new jacket.
She was unsure about keeping a stray.
qs.why: 처음에는 걱정했지만 하룻밤 머물게 허락했다는 흐름에서 추론할 수 있어요.

qs.q: Why did Jun feel a little sad at the end?
o: He did not like the girl.
He had to walk home alone.
qs.why: 강아지가 주인에게 돌아가면 헤어져야 하기 때문이에요.

qs.q: In the passage, “frightened” is closest in meaning to ____.
qs.why: frightened는 겁먹은 상태를 뜻해요.

items.title: Why Honeybees Matter
items.text: Honeybees are small, but they do a very big job. When they fly from flower to flower, collecting sweet liquid, pollen sticks to their legs. This pollen is carried to other flowers, helping plants grow fruit and seeds. Many foods we enjoy, such as apples, almonds and strawberries, depend on this work. Sadly, the number of bees is falling in many places because of lost habitat and certain chemicals. Scientists suggest planting more flowers in gardens and avoiding strong chemicals. Even a few pots on a balcony can give hungry bees a place to feed.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: How to make honey at home with a hive
Why flowers have bright colors and smells
How to keep bees out of a small garden
Why bees matter and how to help them
qs.why: 꿀벌이 식물의 열매 맺기를 돕는다는 점과 꿀벌을 도울 방법을 설명하는 글이에요.

qs.q: What sticks to a bee's legs when it visits flowers?
qs.why: 본문에서 pollen이 다리에 붙는다고 했어요.

qs.q: Why does planting more flowers help bees?
o: It cleans the air for farmers.
qs.why: 꽃은 꿀벌의 먹이 공급처가 된다는 흐름에서 추론할 수 있어요.

qs.q: In the passage, “depend on” is closest in meaning to ____.
qs.why: depend on은 '~에 의존하다, 필요로 하다'라는 뜻이에요.

items.ko: 기진맥진한
items.ex: After the marathon, the runners were completely exhausted.
items.exko: 마라톤이 끝난 뒤 주자들은 완전히 기진맥진했어요.

items.ko: 아주 흥미로운
items.ex: The museum has a fascinating exhibit about ancient ships.
items.exko: 그 박물관에는 고대 선박에 관한 아주 흥미로운 전시가 있어요.

items.ko: 아주 신이 난
items.ex: She was thrilled to win first prize in the contest.
items.exko: 그녀는 대회에서 1등상을 타서 아주 신이 났어요.
